title: Entropy and the second law of thermodynamics
topic: entropy and the second law of thermodynamics
persona_summary: Student arrives with the popular but flawed 'entropy = disorder of a messy room' intuition. They hold a vague hunch about heat flow but cannot articulate why the second law is universal.
turns: Entropy is just a measure of disorder, right? Like how messy a room is.
Hmm, I think energy spreads out somehow when stuff cools down.
OK so heat always flows from hot to cold — is that the second law?
But wait, why does it have to be that way? Couldn't it just go the other way sometimes?
I guess the universe always tends toward more disorder over time.
